source.title: Interpreting and Steering Features in Images

record.tranche_reason: The study uses an SAE to find and manipulate image features for interpretation and image steering. It does not test toy-model superposition or any of the listed LLM claims.
record.gate_note: The post reports SAE feature counts, human ratings of feature-expression icons, and qualitative image-steering outcomes. These concern CLIP image embeddings and image generation, not the listed claims' toy networks, LLMs, or tests of whether SAE features are complete, stable, canonical, or one-dimensional. No version-specific results are recorded.
record.test_reason: The post trains an SAE on CLIP image embeddings and uses its features for interpretation and diffusion steering. It reports feature counts, icon ratings and qualitative steering, not tests of superposition in toy models or LLMs. It does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, canonical or one-dimensional.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is essentially correct. The authors conclude that an SAE on CLIP image embeddings yields many interpretable, steerable features, and that editing them steers diffusion generations predictably and at high quality. They also flag likely undertraining (about 105k dead features) and plan hyperparameter sweeps and better auto-interpretation.
record.recipe_differences: Uses an SAE on CLIP image embeddings and steers a diffusion model; it does not use the toy-network method or measure superposition geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that the chosen activation level (7.5x the maximum embedding activation) did not express some features.

fits_no_version.finding: In CLIP ViT-bigG embeddings, an SAE with 163,840 latents had about 58k alive features, many of them interpretable concepts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAEs recover many interpretable sparse features from vision-encoder embeddings.

fits_no_version.finding: Editing single SAE features (with the reconstruction residual added back) steered Kandinsky 2.2 generations, with no noticeable loss of quality according to qualitative reports.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE features of CLIP embeddings are causally steerable directions for image generation.

fits_no_version.finding: 88% of 200 sampled feature-expression icons were rated as clearly showing the intervention.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Feature-expression icons are a usable preview of SAE feature effects.

record.problems: The authors say the run may be undertrained: approximately 105k features were dead. Reconstruction explained 88% of embedding variance, and the authors note reconstruction could lose aesthetic information. The post reports qualitative steering results and human-rating percentages without uncertainty estimates; it does not describe controlled comparisons for steering quality.
record.rows_left_out: No other claim-relevant outcomes were reported as separately quantified results. The 63% human rating of auto-interpreted labels concerns label quality rather than the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: No toy networks, sparsity sweep or geometry analysis.
No test of capacity competition or dedicated versus shared dimensions.
No test of alternative causes of polysemanticity.
No LLM activations are studied. The SAE recovers interpretable features in CLIP image embeddings only, with no neuron baseline comparison.
No test of completeness, stability across runs, or canonicity. Many features were dead and reconstruction explained 88% of variance.

record.verdict_notes: This is a LessWrong post on a vision model, not an LLM, so it cannot count as V4 evidence, which names LLMs. A commenter (leogao) notes that CLIP neurons are reportedly quite sparse, so a neuron baseline may be strong here; the post does not compare SAE features against neurons. The 63% auto-interpretation label rating is correctly left out.

versions.untested_parts: No toy-network sweep over feature count, sparsity, importance, overlap, or geometry.
No test of capacity pressure, dedicated dimensions, or feature sharing in neurons.
No test of alternative causes of polysemantic neurons.
The study analyzes CLIP image embeddings, not LLM activations; it does not test feature distribution across neurons in LLMs.
The study does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units of a model's representation.
The study edits individual SAE features but does not test whether underlying superposed features are one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: ViT-bigG-14-laion2B-39B-b160k
rows.operation_detail: Counted SAE features with non-zero activation on at least one dataset image.
rows.measure: Features alive on at least one image
rows.value: 35% (58k) of the total of 163k features were alive
rows.note: This is a result about recovering sparse features from image embeddings, not an LLM or superposition test.
rows.check: This is an SAE training statistic (alive-feature count) in a CLIP vision encoder, not an LLM. It bears on no version, and 'observed' has no version to apply to.

rows.subject: human raters
rows.operation_detail: Rated whether feature-expression icons clearly displayed the feature intervention.

conditions.value: 7.5x the max activation in the embeddings

rows.measure: Icons rated as clearly displaying the intervention
rows.note: The post also says this activation value failed to express some features, often concepts such as text or fine compression artifacts.
rows.check: The subject is human raters judging the authors' own icon technique. This evaluates the study's method, not a claim version.

rows.subject: Kandinsky 2.2
rows.operation_detail: Steered image embeddings by editing SAE features and adding back the reconstruction residual, then generated images.

conditions.value: Individual features; the edited feature had a much higher activation value

rows.measure: Qualitative semantic change and generation quality
rows.value: The post reports that edits yielded meaningful conceptual changes and outputs without noticeable degradation of quality; users could perform tasks while maintaining output described as comparably coherent and high quality as the original.
rows.note: Qualitative steering evidence in an image-generation setting; it does not test the listed versions.
rows.check: This is a qualitative steering outcome with no rate of any superposition behaviour. The subject is really the SAE plus the Kandinsky decoder.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
